clue.text: Describe shop supplying food ordered by European

parts.note: a deli is a shop selling prepared foods
ordered in the sense of tidy, arranged neatly

explanation.surface: Someone explains a shop whose food was ordered by a European customer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Food ordered' looks like a single phrase, but 'food' belongs with the shop, and 'ordered' means tidy.
explanation.definitionFit: To delineate something is to outline it precisely, a synonym for describe in detail.

clue.text: Stray remark that's sarcastic about saints

parts.note: a dig is a cutting or sarcastic remark
re means about or concerning, as in business letters
S is the abbreviation for saint, doubled for the plural

explanation.surface: A sarcastic aside about saints that wanders off topic.
explanation.definitionFit: To digress is to wander from the main subject, so it means to stray in talk.

clue.text: Sign in English, nothing lower than pound

parts.note: L is the abbreviation for pound sterling, from Latin libra
O is the round shape of zero, nothing

explanation.surface: An instruction that in English nothing should fall below a pound.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down answer, 'lower than' places E and O beneath L.
explanation.definitionFit: Leo is one of the twelve signs of the zodiac.

clue.text: Refusal, I observe, to accept dry piece of meat

parts.note: no is a refusal

indicators.note: to accept means one piece takes the other in, holding it inside

parts.note: to observe is to see
TT stands for teetotal, someone who stays dry

explanation.surface: A diner refuses, noting a teetotal reluctance over a cut of meat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dry' gives TT, short for teetotal, a crossword convention for someone who avoids alcohol.
explanation.definitionFit: A noisette is a small round boneless cut of lamb or other meat.

clue.text: Republican getting in before now with new element

indicators.note: getting in means one piece enters the middle of another here

parts.note: ago means before the present time

explanation.surface: A Republican gets elected early with a new element in his platform.
explanation.definitionFit: Argon is a chemical element, one of the noble gases.

clue.text: Following change of tone, argue

indicators.note: a change of these letters calls for them to be rearranged into a new order

explanation.surface: After a change of tone, people begin to quarrel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Following' looks like 'after', a link to the rest, but it is the definition, a noun for a group of followers.
explanation.definitionFit: An entourage is a retinue of attendants, a following of people around someone important.

clue.text: Moves to get rid of hard riddles

indicators.note: to get rid of means a piece is removed from the longer word

parts.note: shifts means moves, as a verb
H is the abbreviation for hard, as on pencils

explanation.surface: Someone shifts things around to dispose of tough puzzles.
explanation.walkthrough: 'riddles' looks like a noun for puzzles; it is the verb meaning to pass through a sieve.
explanation.definitionFit: To riddle grain or soil is to pass it through a coarse sieve, so riddles is a synonym.

clue.text: Think suitable appeal should follow rising charges

indicators.note: should follow means this piece comes after the other one
in a down entry, rising means the word is read from the bottom upwards

parts.note: fees are charges for a service
IT means sex appeal, as in the old slang

explanation.surface: Someone judges it fair that an appeal comes after rising charges.
explanation.definitionFit: To see fit is an idiom for deciding something is appropriate to do.

clue.text: Also fuss about amount of heat

indicators.note: about means the first piece goes round the second one

parts.note: a furore is a fuss or uproar
a therm is a unit of heat, used in measuring gas supply

explanation.surface: A complaint over a heating bill: a fuss about the amount of heat used.
explanation.definitionFit: Furthermore is an adverb meaning in addition, a synonym for also.

clue.text: Vault, top to bottom, getting into state eventually

indicators.note: getting into means a piece enters inside the other

parts.note: to state is to say

indicators.note: in a down entry, top to bottom means the first letter moves to the end

parts.note: a dome is a vaulted roof

explanation.surface: A vault is turned upside down as it enters a state at last.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down answer the top letter is the first, so 'top to bottom' sends it to the end, making OMED.
explanation.definitionFit: Someday is an adverb for at some future time, one sense of eventually.

clue.text: Complimentary section on work entered by learner

entered by means another piece is put inside this combination

parts.note: to go is to work or function, as a machine goes
L is the abbreviation for learner, as on learner-driver plates
a wing is a section of a building

explanation.surface: A flattering report about part of a building entered by a trainee.
explanation.definitionFit: A glowing report is full of praise, so glowing means highly complimentary.

clue.text: Proposition, explosive, to cut rent by millions

indicators.note: to cut means a piece is thrust into the middle of another

parts.note: tore means rent, past tense of rend
HE is the abbreviation for high explosive
M is the abbreviation for million

explanation.surface: A proposal that explosives might cut rent by millions.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rent' looks like a noun for money paid; it is the past tense of rend.
explanation.definitionFit: A theorem is a statement to be proved, a proposition in mathematics.

clue.text: Cross in dispute, losing head before end of volatile display

indicators.note: in means one piece is placed inside another
losing head means the first letter is removed

parts.note: a feud is a long-running dispute
X is the shape of a cross

indicators.note: end of means the last letter of the following word

explanation.surface: A heated quarrel loses its leader before a volatile scene.
explanation.definitionFit: To exude confidence is to display it openly, a figurative use.

clue.text: Simple heart of community, pleasant and calm, up above a river

indicators.note: heart of means the central letter of the word

parts.note: nice means pleasant

indicators.note: in a down entry, up means the word is read from the bottom upwards

parts.note: a lull is a calm period

explanation.surface: A simple community at peace, with a calm river flowing above it.
explanation.definitionFit: A unicellular organism consists of a single cell, the simplest form of life.

clue.text: Sustained fourth of injuries in hard round and lost

indicators.note: in means a letter is placed inside the other piece
round means the word is turned back to front

parts.note: iron means hard or unyielding

parts.note: shed means lost or cast off, as weight is shed

explanation.walkthrough: 'round' turns IRON into NORI and 'in' puts U inside it.

clue.text: Trace cousin originally at home in quiet area

indicators.note: in means these letters are placed inside the other piece

parts.note: still means quiet and calm

indicators.note: originally means the first letter of the word

parts.note: in means at home

explanation.surface: A trace of a cousin who used to be at home in a quiet district.
explanation.definitionFit: A scintilla is a tiny amount, a trace or iota.

clue.text: Record most of song on time with sovereign power

parts.note: a log is a record, as of a ship's voyage

indicators.note: most of means the last letter of the word is dropped

parts.note: an aria is a song in an opera
HM stands for His or Her Majesty, the sovereign

explanation.surface: An account of a song played for a monarch with absolute power.
explanation.walkthrough: 'power' looks like royal might; it is the mathematical sense, an exponent.
explanation.definitionFit: A logarithm is the exponent, or power, to which a base must be raised to give a number.

clue.text: Become irritated and fight

definitions.meaning: nerves or tempers wear thin and become strained

explanation.definitionFit: Tempers fray when strained, and a fray is a noisy fight or brawl.

clue.text: Extraordinary call, ignoring leader, to arrest sergeant?

indicators.note: to arrest means to catch and hold a piece inside
ignoring leader means the first letter is removed

parts.note: to summon is to call
a sergeant is an example of an NCO, a non-commissioned officer

explanation.walkthrough: The question mark shows sergeant is only an example of an NCO.

clue.text: Regular pieces of advice at assembly

indicators.note: regular pieces of means every second letter is taken from the words

explanation.surface: Advice given at a meeting is passed on in regular portions.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Regular pieces' suggests a meal plan, but it picks even letters of 'advice at'.
explanation.definitionFit: A diet is a formal legislative assembly, as in some European parliaments.

clue.text: Under endless obligation, left overwhelmed by great failure

indicators.note: in a down entry, under means this piece comes below the other
endless means the last letter is removed

parts.note: a debt is an obligation

indicators.note: overwhelmed by means one piece is covered inside another

parts.note: ace means great or excellent

explanation.surface: Under endless obligations, someone who left is swamped by a huge disaster.
explanation.walkthrough: 'great failure' reads as one phrase, but 'great' is ACE, so failure alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A debacle is a sudden, humiliating collapse, a fiasco or failure.

clue.text: Novice good and fresh here on service

indicators.note: fresh means these letters are made anew in another order

parts.note: RN stands for Royal Navy, one of the armed services

explanation.surface: A promising new recruit, fresh and here on military service.
explanation.definitionFit: A greenhorn is an inexperienced newcomer, a synonym for novice.

clue.text: Note place held by wit in puzzle

indicators.note: held by means these letters go inside the other piece

parts.note: nous means common sense or wit
PL is the abbreviation for place, as in street names

explanation.surface: A note on a place held by a clever person in a puzzle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'puzzle' is a verb here: to bewilder.
explanation.definitionFit: To nonplus someone is to baffle them, so puzzle is a synonym.

clue.text: Strong support in secret

indicators.note: in means a piece is placed inside the other

parts.note: sly means secretive or furtive
a tee is a support for a golf ball

explanation.surface: Strong support given in secret.
explanation.definitionFit: Steely means hard and resolute, a figurative sense of strong.

clue.text: Worried artist required to fill poster having two sides

indicators.note: to fill means these letters go into the middle of the other piece

parts.note: a bill is a poster, as in bill-sticking
ate means worried, as in what's eating you
RA stands for Royal Academician, an artist

explanation.walkthrough: 'Worried' looks like an anagram signal, but it is ATE, past tense of eat in its sense of to trouble.
explanation.definitionFit: Bilateral means involving two sides, as in bilateral talks.

clue.text: Substitute having look around with uncertain expression

parts.note: lo is an old word meaning look
C is the abbreviation for circa, meaning around
um is a sound of hesitation

explanation.surface: A stand-in looks around and hesitates.
explanation.walkthrough: 'around' looks like a container signal but gives C for circa.
explanation.definitionFit: A locum is a doctor or priest standing in for another, a substitute.

clue.text: Quantity of water over sponge? Not litres

parts.note: O is the cricket abbreviation for over

indicators.note: not means a letter is removed from the word

parts.note: to sponge is to clean

explanation.surface: How much water fits in a sponge, without counting litres?
explanation.definitionFit: An ocean is a vast body of seawater.

clue.text: Vicar back with coverage from religious group's channel

indicators.note: coverage from means the other piece is wrapped inside

parts.note: a cult is a religious group

parts.note: Rev is short for Reverend, a vicar's title

explanation.definitionFit: A culvert is a tunnel or drain carrying water under a road, a channel.

clue.text: Funny business, claim being falsified

parts.note: CO is the abbreviation for company, a business

indicators.note: being falsified means the word's letters are altered into a false order

explanation.surface: A firm's claim is falsified, which is amusing.
explanation.definitionFit: Comical means causing laughter, a synonym for funny.

clue.text: Sound made by dove getting crumbs

definitions.meaning: the soft murmuring call of a pigeon or dove
crumbs is an exclamation of surprise, as is the other word

explanation.surface: A dove makes a sound while picking up crumbs.

clue.text: Rely on revision to secure top mark soon

on revision means the letters are revised into a new order

explanation.definitionFit: Early means at a near time, before long, a synonym for soon.

in retreat means the word is read backwards

parts.note: a sum is a quantity
an omen is a warning sign

explanation.surface: An army in retreat carries a warning to the major.
explanation.walkthrough: 'major' looks like an officer; it is an adjective meaning important. 'in retreat' turns SUM into MUS.
explanation.definitionFit: Momentous means of great importance, a synonym for major.
